quarterly_data.signal: IBM (10-K): 2025 revenue was $67,535 million, up 7.6% (6.1% adjusted for currency), with gross margin 58.2% and net income $10,593 million; Software revenue $29,962 million (+10.6%; segment profit margin 33.1%), Consulting $21,055 million (+1.8%) and Infrastructure $15,718 million (+12.1%). Within Infrastructure, Hybrid Infrastructure revenue of $10,618 million rose 19.1%, with IBM Z up 51.7% on the strong performance of z17 and Power improving in the second half on the launch of Power11; Infrastructure servers revenue was $5,410 million (2024: $3,693 million). Software annual recurring revenue was $23.6 billion at year end 2025; Consulting signings were $21,757 million (-13.3%), with trailing book-to-bill of 1.03 and backlog of $31.9 billion at year end 2025. Free cash flow was $14.7 billion after $1.6 billion of net capital expenditures.

IBM (10-K): R&D expense rose 11.2% in 2025 to $8,316 million, driven by investments in AI, hybrid cloud and quantum; IBM says its new Spyre AI accelerator powers the AI capabilities of z17 and Power11 systems. IBM says that, to expand client choice and speed in using AI, it strengthened its AI ecosystem through partnerships with NVIDIA, Anthropic, Groq and AMD (no supply or customer terms stated). Certain IBM businesses rely on a single or a limited number of suppliers, including for server processor technology for certain semiconductors.
